match.reason: The bank point 'Mitosis' gives only an overview of the process and its purpose and never names or describes the stages (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase), so the new point teaches content the existing card does not cover.

draft.title: Stages of mitosis
card: Before mitosis, each chromosome is copied. It then has two identical sister chromatids joined together. Mitosis shares these copies equally between two nuclei.
Prophase
the chromosomes coil up and become visible. The nuclear membrane breaks down.
Metaphase
the chromosomes line up across the middle of the cell, attached to spindle fibres.
Anaphase and telophase
in anaphase, spindle fibres pull sister chromatids to opposite ends, and each becomes a chromosome. In telophase, a nuclear membrane forms around each set, giving two identical nuclei.
draft.remember: Mitosis ends with two identical nuclei, because sister chromatids are pulled apart.

a.q: During which stage of mitosis are sister chromatids pulled to opposite ends of the cell?
a.why: In anaphase the spindle fibres pull the sister chromatids apart. In metaphase they are only lined up across the middle and are still joined.
a.clue: The chromatids split and move apart in this stage.

b.q: A student views a dividing onion root cell. The chromosomes are lined up across the middle of the cell and the nuclear membrane is absent. Which stage is this?
b.why: Chromosomes lined up across the middle of the cell, attached to spindle fibres, show metaphase. Prophase also has no nuclear membrane, but the chromosomes are not yet lined up in the middle.
b.clue: Look at where the chromosomes are sitting in the cell.

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'Prophase also has no nuclear membrane', but the card says the nuclear membrane breaks down during prophase. It is still present at the start of prophase and only gone by the end. A better wording: 'By the end of prophase the nuclear membrane has broken down, but the chromosomes are not yet lined up in the middle.'

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, with one clear right answer each. The only problem is in why (b), which says prophase has no nuclear membrane, when the card says it breaks down during prophase.
